docs.title: Todo App Documentation
docs.text: Welcome to the Todo App documentation! This is a feature-rich Android todo list application with recurring tasks, notifications, calendar views, and home screen widget support.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Todo App helps you manage your daily tasks with powerful features like:

  • ✅ Smart scheduling with recurring tasks
  • 📅 Interactive calendar and weekly waterfall view
  • 🔔 Reliable notification system
  • 📱 Home screen widgets
  • 💾 Local data storage with history tracking
  • 🎨 Material Design UI

docs.text:

  • Database: Room (SQLite)
  • Async: Kotlin Coroutines + Flow

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
The fastest way to get started is using Docker:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/yourusername/todoapp.git
cd todoapp

# Build with Docker
chmod +x docker-build.sh
./docker-build.sh debug

# Install to device
./docker-build.sh install

For detailed instructions, see the Building guide.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
1. User Action → View (Activity/Fragment)
  2. View → ViewModel (via method calls)
  3. ViewModel → Repository (data operations)
  4. Repository → DAO (database queries)
  5. DAO → Database (Room)
  6. Database → DAO → Repository (via Flow)
  7. Repository → ViewModel (LiveData updates)
  8. ViewModel → View (UI updates via observers)

docs.title: Repository Pattern
docs.text: Centralizes data access logic and provides clean API to ViewModel.

docs.title: Observer Pattern

docs.title: Quick Start with Helper Script
docs.text:
The easiest way to build with Docker:

# Make the script executable (first time only)
chmod +x docker-build.sh

# Build debug APK
./docker-build.sh debug

# Build release APK
./docker-build.sh release

# Clean build
./docker-build.sh clean

# Run unit tests
./docker-build.sh test

# Install to device
./docker-build.sh install

# See all options
./docker-build.sh help

The script automatically:

  • Creates and uses a Gradle cache volume for faster builds
  • Shows colored output for easier reading
  • Tells you where to find built APKs
  • Handles common errors

docs.title: Manual Docker Commands
docs.text:
If you prefer to run Docker commands directly:

Build debug APK:

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -w /app thyrlian/android-sdk:latest \
  ./gradlew assembleDebug

Build release APK:

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -w /app thyrlian/android-sdk:latest \
  ./gradlew assembleRelease

Clean and build:

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -w /app thyrlian/android-sdk:latest \
  ./gradlew clean assembleDebug

Speed up builds with Gradle cache:

# Create a named volume for Gradle cache
docker volume create gradle-cache

# Use it in your builds
docker run --rm \
  -v "$(pwd)":/app \
  -v gradle-cache:/root/.gradle \
  -w /app \
  thyrlian/android-sdk:latest \
  ./gradlew assembleDebug

Find your built APK:

After building, APKs are located at:

  • Debug: app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
  • Release: app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk

Install on connected device:

# Install debug APK (requires ADB installed locally)
adb install app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk

# Or install release APK
adb install app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk

docs.title: Using Docker Compose
docs.text:
Create a docker-compose.yml file:

version: '3.8'
services:
  android-build:
    image: thyrlian/android-sdk:latest
    volumes:
      - .:/app
      - gradle-cache:/root/.gradle
    working_dir: /app
    command: ./gradlew assembleDebug

volumes:
  gradle-cache:

Then run:

docker-compose run android-build

docs.title: Quick Reference: Common Docker Build Commands
docs.text:
Build and install in one step:

# Build debug APK
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -v gradle-cache:/root/.gradle -w /app \
  thyrlian/android-sdk:latest ./gradlew assembleDebug

# Install to device (requires ADB locally)
adb install -r app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk

Check build version:

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -w /app thyrlian/android-sdk:latest \
  ./gradlew -q printVersionName

List all Gradle tasks:

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -w /app thyrlian/android-sdk:latest \
  ./gradlew tasks

Build with logs:

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -v gradle-cache:/root/.gradle -w /app \
  thyrlian/android-sdk:latest ./gradlew assembleDebug --info

docs.title: Troubleshooting Docker Builds
docs.text:
Build is slow - Use the Gradle cache volume as shown above - First builds download dependencies (slow) - Subsequent builds are much faster

Permission denied - On Linux, you may need to add --user $(id -u):$(id -g)

Out of disk space - Clean up with docker system prune -a

Gradle daemon issues - Add --no-daemon flag to gradle commands

docs.title: Automated Builds with GitHub Actions
docs.text:
The project includes automated CI/CD workflows:

On every push/PR to main:

  • Automatically builds debug and release APKs
  • APKs available as artifacts in GitHub Actions (30 day retention)
  • Download from: Actions → Latest Run → Artifacts

On version tags (e.g., v1.0.0):

  • Automatically creates GitHub Release with APK attached
  • See .github/workflows/README.md for setup instructions

To create a release:

git tag v1.0.0
git push origin v1.0.0

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: The app uses Room for local data persistence with SQLite.

docs.title: TodoEntity Table
docs.text:
Primary table storing all todo items.

Column Type Description id Long Primary key (auto-generated) text String Todo text content isCompleted Boolean Completion status dueDateTime Long? Due date/time timestamp in milliseconds (nullable) recurrencePattern RecurrencePattern JSON serialized recurrence configuration createdAt Long Creation timestamp lastModifiedAt Long Last modification timestamp notificationEnabled Boolean Whether notifications are enabled for this todo parentTodoId Long? Link to original todo for recurring instances (nullable)

docs.title: RecurrencePattern Structure
docs.text:
Stored as JSON via Room type converters:

data class RecurrencePattern(
    val type: RecurrenceType,           // NONE, HOURLY, DAILY, WEEKLY, MONTHLY, YEARLY
    val interval: Int = 1,              // Every N units
    val daysOfWeek: Set<Int> = emptySet(),  // For weekly: 1=Mon, 7=Sun
    val dayOfMonth: Int? = null,        // For monthly: specific day
    val endDate: Long? = null           // When recurrence ends
)

docs.title: TodoCompletionHistory Table
docs.text:
Tracks completion history for reporting and analytics.

Column Type Description id Long Primary key (auto-generated) todoId Long Reference to TodoEntity id completedAt Long Completion timestamp dueDateTime Long? When it was originally due (nullable) text String Snapshot of todo text at completion time

docs.title: Common DAO Queries
docs.text:
Get all todos: 

@Query("SELECT * FROM todos ORDER BY dueDateTime ASC, createdAt DESC")
fun getAllTodos(): Flow<List<TodoEntity>>

Get today's todos: 

@Query("SELECT * FROM todos WHERE date(dueDateTime/1000, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') = date('now', 'localtime') ORDER BY dueDateTime ASC")
fun getTodayTodos(): Flow<List<TodoEntity>>

Get todos by specific date: 

@Query("SELECT * FROM todos WHERE date(dueDateTime/1000, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') = date(:date/1000, 'unixepoch', 'localtime') ORDER BY dueDateTime ASC")
fun getTodosByDate(date: Long): Flow<List<TodoEntity>>

Get due todos for notifications: 

@Query("SELECT * FROM todos WHERE dueDateTime <= :currentTime AND notificationEnabled = 1")
suspend fun getDueTodos(currentTime: Long): List<TodoEntity>

docs.title: Type Converters
docs.text: Room uses custom type converters for complex types:

docs.title: RecurrencePattern Converter
docs.text:
class Converters {
    @TypeConverter
    fun fromRecurrencePattern(value: RecurrencePattern): String {
        return Gson().toJson(value)
    }

    @TypeConverter
    fun toRecurrencePattern(value: String): RecurrencePattern {
        return Gson().fromJson(value, RecurrencePattern::class.java)
    }
}

docs.title: Database Migrations
docs.text:
Currently using version 1 with no migrations.

Future migrations should: - Preserve user data - Handle schema changes gracefully - Include rollback strategies

docs.title: Recurring Todos
docs.text:
Recurring todos use a parent-child relationship:

  • Parent Todo: Original todo with recurrence pattern
  • Child Todos: Generated occurrences with parentTodoId pointing to parent

When a recurring todo is completed: 1. Mark current instance as complete 2. Create next occurrence based on recurrence pattern 3. Link to parent via parentTodoId

docs.title: Completion History
docs.text: Each completion creates a history record: - Tracks when todo was completed - Preserves snapshot of todo state - Used for completion statistics

docs.title: Indexes
docs.text:
• Primary key index on id (automatic)
  • Consider adding index on dueDateTime for large datasets
  • Consider adding index on parentTodoId for recurring todos

docs.title: Query Optimization
docs.text:
• Use Flow for reactive queries (efficient)
  • Limit results when displaying lists
  • Use paging for very large datasets (future enhancement)

docs.text:

docs.title: Required Permissions
docs.text:
The app requires the following permissions:

  • POST_NOTIFICATIONS: Show todo notifications (Android 13+)
  • SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM: Schedule exact alarm for due date reminders (Android 12+)
  • USE_EXACT_ALARM: Use exact alarm API
  • WAKE_LOCK: Wake device for notifications
  • RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED: Reschedule notifications after device restart
  • REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS: Request exemption from battery optimization

docs.title: Setting Up Notifications
docs.text: To ensure you receive notifications when your phone is idle or screen is off:

docs.title: 1. Grant Notification Permission (Android 13+)
docs.text:
Automatic: - The app will request this on first launch

Manual: - Go to: Settings → Apps → Todo App → Notifications → Allow

docs.title: 2. Enable Exact Alarms (Android 12+)
docs.text:
Guided Setup: - The app will guide you to the settings

Manual: - Go to: Settings → Apps → Todo App → Alarms & reminders → Allow - This ensures notifications appear exactly when todos are due

docs.title: 3. Disable Battery Optimization
docs.text:
Critical for Pixel Phones

This is the most important step for Pixel phones and devices with aggressive battery management!

Automatic: - The app will prompt you to exempt it from battery optimization

Manual: - Settings → Apps → Todo App → Battery → Unrestricted

docs.title: 4. Additional Pixel-Specific Settings
docs.text:
For Google Pixel phones, additional steps may be needed:

  1. Battery Optimization

  2. Settings → Apps → Todo App → Battery → Battery optimization → Not optimized

  3. Adaptive Preferences

  4. Settings → Battery → Adaptive preferences → Disable for Todo App

  5. Special App Access

  6. Settings → Apps → Special app access → Battery optimization → Todo App → Don't optimize

docs.title: Not Receiving Notifications When Phone Is Idle
docs.text:
1. ✅ Check that all three permissions above are granted
  2. ✅ Verify notification settings: Settings → Notifications → App notifications → Todo App
  3. ✅ Ensure "Do Not Disturb" mode isn't blocking notifications
  4. ✅ Restart the app after granting battery optimization exemption
  5. ✅ Create a test todo due in 2-3 minutes to verify notifications work

docs.title: Notifications Appear Late
docs.text:
• Check battery optimization settings
  • Ensure "Alarms & reminders" permission is granted
  • Restart device after changing settings

docs.title: No Notification Sound/Vibration
docs.text:
• Check notification channel settings
  • Settings → Apps → Todo App → Notifications → Todo Reminders
  • Ensure sound and vibration are enabled

docs.title: Notifications Don't Wake Screen
docs.text:
• Check that WAKE_LOCK permission is granted
  • Some devices require additional settings to wake screen

docs.title: Using the Test Notification Feature
docs.text:
1. Open the app
  2. Menu → Test Notification
  3. A notification should appear immediately
  4. Swipe down to expand and see the "Mark Complete" button

This helps verify that: - Notification permissions are working - Notification channels are configured - Notification actions work correctly

docs.title: Creating a Real Test
docs.text:
1. Add a new todo
  2. Set due date/time to 2-3 minutes from now
  3. Enable notifications
  4. Save the todo
  5. Lock your phone and wait
  6. Notification should appear at the exact time

docs.title: When to Grant Permissions
docs.text:
• Grant notification permission to receive reminders
  • Grant exact alarm permission for precise timing
  • Disable battery optimization for reliable background notifications

docs.title: Privacy Considerations
docs.text: All permissions are used exclusively for: - Scheduling and displaying todo notifications - Keeping the app alive in the background for timely alerts - No data is collected or shared

docs.title: Android 13+ (API 33)
docs.text:
• Runtime notification permission required
  • Must explicitly request POST_NOTIFICATIONS

docs.title: Android 12+ (API 31)
docs.text:
• Exact alarm permission required
  • Must request SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM

docs.title: Android 7.0-11 (API 24-30)
docs.text:
• Battery optimization exemption recommended
  • No runtime notification permission needed

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: The project includes comprehensive instrumented tests using Espresso with automatic test data seeding.

docs.title: Test Data Seeding
docs.text:
All instrumented tests automatically seed sample data before running. This ensures consistent and reliable test execution both locally and in CI/CD pipelines.

See the androidTest README for complete seeding documentation.

docs.title: Option 1: Using Docker (Recommended)
docs.text: Docker provides a consistent environment with Java and Android SDK pre-configured.

docs.title: Option 2: Local Installation
docs.text:
• Java 17 (JDK): Required for building and running tests
  • Android SDK: Platform SDK 34, Build Tools, Platform Tools
  • Android Emulator or physical device (API 24+)

docs.title: Running Tests with Docker
docs.text:
Unit Tests (no emulator required):

# Run unit tests
docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -w /app thyrlian/android-sdk:latest ./gradlew test

# View results
open app/build/reports/tests/testDebugUnitTest/index.html

Build APK for Testing:

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/app -w /app thyrlian/android-sdk:latest \
  ./gradlew assembleDebug assembleDebugAndroidTest

docs.title: Running Instrumented Tests
docs.text:
# Verify device is connected
adb devices

# Run all instrumented tests
./gradlew connectedAndroidTest

# Run a specific test class
./gradlew connectedAndroidTest \
  -Pandroid.testInstrumentationRunnerArguments.class=com.example.todoapp.TodoSelectionTest

docs.title: Test Coverage
docs.text:
• TodoSelectionTest - Visual feedback and selection persistence
  • TodoSelectionWithDataTest - Selection with guaranteed data
  • TodoCompletionPersistenceTest - Completion state persistence
  • CalendarWaterfallTest - Weekly waterfall calendar view

See the androidTest README for details.

docs.title: Automated Testing with GitHub Actions
docs.text:
Tests automatically run on every pull request and push to main:

  • Unit tests run on Ubuntu
  • Instrumented tests run on Android emulator (API 29)
  • Test results available as artifacts for 30 days

docs.title: Adding a Todo
docs.text:
1. Tap the floating action button (FAB) in the bottom right
  2. Enter the todo text
  3. (Optional) Set due date and time using the date/time pickers
  4. (Optional) Configure recurrence pattern:
  5. Select recurrence type (None, Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Yearly)
  6. Set interval (e.g., every 2 days)
  7. For weekly: select specific days of the week
  8. Enable/disable notifications
  9. Tap "Save"

docs.title: Editing a Todo
docs.text:
1. Tap on any todo item in the list
  2. The edit screen opens with all current values pre-filled
  3. Modify any fields you want to change
  4. Tap "Update" to save changes
  5. Changes are reflected immediately in all views

docs.title: Managing Todos
docs.text:
• Complete: Tap the checkbox next to a todo
  • Edit: Tap anywhere on a todo item to edit its details
  • Delete: Tap the trash icon
  • View Details: Todos show due date and recurrence info below the text

docs.title: Today's Todos (Default)
docs.text:
Shows only todos due today for focused task management.

  • Access: Launches by default, or Menu → Today's Todos

docs.title: All Todos
docs.text:
View all todos regardless of due date.

  • Access: Menu → All Todos

docs.title: Calendar View
docs.text:
Visual calendar interface showing todos across time.

  • Access: Menu → Calendar View
  • Tap any date to see todos for that day
  • Navigate between months
  • See which dates have todos

docs.title: Weekly Waterfall View
docs.text:
View the current week in a flowing waterfall layout.

  • 7 vertical day columns
  • Todos cascade down each day by time
  • Color-coded status (green=complete, blue=pending, red=overdue)
  • Navigate between weeks with arrow buttons
  • Horizontal scrolling to view all days

docs.title: Hide Completed
docs.text:
Toggle to hide/show completed todos:

  • Access: Menu → Hide Completed (checkable option)
  • Applies to all view modes (Today, All Todos, Calendar)
  • Useful for focusing on active tasks
  • State persists while app is running

docs.title: Todo List Widget
docs.text:
1. Long press on home screen
  2. Select "Widgets"
  3. Find "Todo App" → "Today's Todos" widget
  4. Drag to desired location
  5. Widget shows today's todos and updates automatically

Widget Features: - View today's todos from home screen - Check off items without opening app - Auto-updates when todos change - Resizable to fit your layout

docs.title: Calendar Widget
docs.text:
1. Long press on home screen
  2. Select "Widgets"
  3. Find "Todo App" → "Calendar" widget
  4. Drag to desired location

Widget Features: - Current month calendar view - Days with todos show dot indicators - Today highlighted in purple - Shows up to 5 of today's todos below calendar - Tap to open app

docs.title: Seeding Sample Data
docs.text:
For testing or demonstration purposes:

  1. Open the app
  2. Tap Menu (three dots)
  3. Select "Seed Sample Todos"
  4. Confirm the dialog
  5. ~25 sample todos will be added across the current week

This is useful for: - Testing the waterfall calendar view - Demonstrating features - Development and testing

docs.title: Recurring Tasks
docs.text:
• Set up recurring tasks once and they auto-create
  • Complete a recurring todo to generate the next occurrence
  • Edit the parent to change all future occurrences

docs.title: Notifications
docs.text:
• Enable notifications per todo for important deadlines
  • Notifications appear at the exact due time
  • Mark todos complete directly from notifications
  • See Permissions for reliable notification setup

docs.title: Organization
docs.text:
• Use the "Hide Completed" filter to focus on active tasks
  • Switch to "All Todos" to review everything
  • Use the calendar view for long-term planning
  • Use the waterfall view to see your week at a glance

docs.title: Home Screen Widgets
docs.text: The app provides two home screen widgets for quick access to your todos.

docs.title: Todo List Widget
docs.text: View and interact with today's todos directly from your home screen.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Quick Access: View today's todos without opening the app
  • Check Off Items: Mark todos complete with a single tap
  • Auto-Update: Widget refreshes automatically when todos change
  • Resizable: Adjust widget size to fit your home screen layout
  • Empty State: Shows helpful message when no todos exist

docs.title: Adding the Widget
docs.text:
1. Long press on your home screen
  2. Select "Widgets" from the menu
  3. Find "Todo App" → "Today's Todos" widget
  4. Drag the widget to your desired location
  5. Resize as needed by dragging the corners

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: The widget: - Displays todos due today - Updates when you complete, add, or edit todos - Uses a ListView for efficient scrolling - Shows checkboxes for quick completion - Taps on todo text open the app for editing

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text: Provider: TodoWidget.kt Service: TodoWidgetService.kt Layout: widget_todo_list.xml, widget_todo_item.xml

docs.title: Calendar Widget
docs.text: Monthly calendar view with todo indicators and today's todo list.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Monthly View: See the entire current month at a glance
  • Visual Indicators: Days with todos show a small dot indicator
  • Today Highlight: Current day highlighted in purple/blue
  • Quick Todo List: Shows up to 5 of today's todos below the calendar
  • Tap to Open: Tap the header to open the calendar view in the app
  • Compact Design: Fits nicely on home screen while showing useful info
  • Day Selection: Tap any day to see todos for that date (opens app)

docs.title: Adding the Widget
docs.text:
1. Long press on your home screen
  2. Select "Widgets" from the menu
  3. Find "Todo App" → "Calendar" widget
  4. Drag the widget to your desired location
  5. The widget is fixed-size and optimized for readability

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: The widget: - Shows current month's calendar grid - Indicates which days have todos with dots - Lists today's todos below the calendar - Updates automatically when todos change - Opens the calendar view when tapped

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text: Provider: CalendarWidget.kt Grid Service: CalendarWidgetGridService.kt Todo Service: CalendarWidgetTodoService.kt Layout: widget_calendar.xml, widget_calendar_day.xml, widget_calendar_todo_item.xml

docs.title: Automatic Updates
docs.text: Widgets update automatically when: - A todo is added, edited, or deleted - A todo is marked complete/incomplete - The date changes (for "today's" todos)

docs.title: Manual Updates
docs.text: Widgets can be manually refreshed by: - Removing and re-adding the widget - Restarting the device - Opening the app (triggers update)

docs.title: Update Frequency
docs.text:
• On Data Change: Immediate update via AppWidgetManager
  • Periodic: System handles periodic updates
  • On Boot: Widgets restore on device restart

docs.title: Todo List Widget
docs.text:
• Size: Works best in 2x2 or larger
  • Placement: Put on main home screen for quick access
  • Usage: Great for daily task management

docs.title: Calendar Widget
docs.text:
• Size: Fixed size optimized for 4x3 grid
  • Placement: Secondary screen or tablet
  • Usage: Great for weekly/monthly planning

docs.title: Todo List Widget
docs.text:
• Shows today's todos only
  • Limited to screen size (scrollable)
  • No inline editing (opens app)
  • Checkbox action only for completion

docs.title: Calendar Widget
docs.text:
• Shows current month only
  • Maximum 5 todos displayed
  • No month navigation on widget
  • Fixed size layout

docs.title: Widget Not Updating
docs.text:
1. Open the app to trigger an update
  2. Remove and re-add the widget
  3. Check app permissions
  4. Restart device

docs.title: Widget Shows No Data
docs.text:
1. Ensure you have todos created
  2. Check that todos have due dates
  3. For calendar widget, ensure todos are in current month
  4. Open app to verify data exists

docs.title: Widget Looks Broken
docs.text:
1. Remove widget
  2. Clear app cache (Settings → Apps → Todo App → Storage → Clear Cache)
  3. Re-add widget
  4. If problem persists, reinstall app

docs.title: Widget Communication
docs.text: Widgets communicate with the app via: - Intent Filters: For update broadcasts - PendingIntents: For user interactions - RemoteViews: For UI updates

docs.title: Data Access
docs.text: Widgets access data via: - TodoDatabase: Direct Room database access - Coroutines: Asynchronous data loading - RemoteViewsService: For list data

docs.title: Testing Widgets
docs.text: To test widgets: 1. Use "Seed Sample Todos" from app menu 2. Add widget to home screen 3. Verify data appears correctly 4. Test interactions (checkboxes, taps) 5. Test updates by modifying todos in app
